_about: Post-apocalypse: after the fall, scavenging, settlements, and what is worth rebuilding. Story axes for story_gen.py. Each axis is rolled on its own; an entry is a string (weight 1) or {v, w, decay}. All text is our own.

the_end: a sickness that took the cities first
the rains that would not stop
the sun went pale and the crops failed
the machines that ran everything just stopped
the sea came in over the deltas
a fungus that grew through everything
a quiet night when the grid never came back
how_long: the ashes are still warm, one month on
five years, and the canned food is running out
a generation, and children ask what a city was
so long the old world is only stories
ten years, long enough for new borders
three harvests since the last broadcast
long enough that the rust has won
settlement: a fortified school with a rooftop garden
a floating village of lashed-together barges on the chao phraya
a monastery that took everyone in
a highway overpass walled in with buses
a dam town that still has power, barely
a mall turned into a market with its own laws
a hill temple above the flood line in northern laos
a ring of farms around an old prison
scarcity: clean water that does not make you sick
diesel for the one working pump
someone who can still read the old manuals
faction: a convoy that trades fuel for people
a cult that says the fall was a cleansing
the last soldiers still following old orders
a family that owns the only well
scavenger crews who strip the dead cities
a council of elders who ban the old tech
a river fleet that taxes every crossing
doctors who choose who gets treated
relic: a working solar panel, half cracked
a seed vault key on a dead man's neck
a library in a sealed basement
a hospital generator that needs one part
a map of underground water drawn before the fall
a satellite phone that sometimes hears voices
a cold storage room full of vaccines
a train engine in a jungle depot outside hat yai

cliches: the bunker of rich people who survived
a radio voice promising a safe zone
